claims.claim: The query is a sulfamoylbenzoic acid loop diuretic (furosemide-type); bumetanide, the same pharmacologic class, has absolute oral bioavailability of 95% in patients with cirrhosis, providing direct same-condition, same-class evidence for F >= 20%.

Other cirrhosis-context records also show high oral bioavailability: metoclopramide 79-82% and tolfenamic acid about 91-100%, supporting that the cirrhosis condition in this evidence set is associated with high F.

The closest structural analog, azosemide, has absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 20.4% in healthy fasted humans, which is above the 20% threshold; although this is a different condition and a borderline value, it does not provide affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

The physicochemical prior (low logD, high TPSA, full ionization) suggests poor passive permeability, but it is not an affirmative endpoint measurement and is outweighed by the direct human bioavailability records.

evidence_gaps: No direct furosemide-specific oral bioavailability record is present in the supplied cards; the decision relies on same-class (bumetanide) and structural-analog (azosemide) transfer.
The azosemide record is from healthy fasted subjects, not cirrhosis, and its F of 20.4% is close to the threshold, leaving uncertainty about the magnitude of furosemide's F in cirrhosis.
The physicochemical prior indicates poor passive permeability, but no direct absorption or first-pass measurement for the query is supplied.
Cirrhosis severity, formulation, and dose effects on furosemide absorption are not specified in the evidence.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%) because the most relevant same-class, same-condition evidence (bumetanide in cirrhosis, F=95%) and multiple cirrhosis-context records support high oral bioavailability; the closest structural analog azosemide has F=20.4% (above threshold), and no affirmative evidence supports F<20%. Confidence is moderate due to reliance on transfer and the borderline analog value.
